scholar: The Tamhīd consensus (Ṭabāṭabāʾī, Āshtiyānī, Javādī Āmulī, Nasr, Ziai), as characterized by Melvin-Koushki
title: The mystical philosopher
summary: Melvin-Koushki builds this 'de facto consensus' from the Tamhīd al-Qawāʿid, a staple of Imami seminary curricula: Ibn Turka as a synthesizer of Ibn Sīnā, Suhravardī and Ibn ʿArabī on absolute being, midway between Ṭūsī or Ibn ʿArabī and Mullā Ṣadrā, and so a precursor of the school of Isfahan. No scholar holds it in exactly these words, and the phases are the periodisation the reading needs, not any scholar's own.
